newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Eagle to spin off Tai Shan unit.
newsitem.headline: Great Eagle to spin off Tai Shan unit.

text.p: Great Eagle Holdings Ltd said on Monday it would spin off its Tai Shan Properties Ltd unit raising between HK$2.31 billion and HK$2.50 billion.

Following a group reorganisation, Tai Shan would concentrate on the development and ownership of primarily Grade A office and commercial properties which were previously conducted by various subsidiaries of Great Eagle, the company said in a statement.
Shares in the company would be offered in a Hong Kong public offering and also to international professional and institutional investors in Hong Kong, the United States and elsewhere, it added.
Following the Tai Shan offering, Great Eagle said it would own 73.15 percent of the unit.
"After the reorganisation and combined offering, Great Eagle will focus its resources primarily on the development of and investment in residential properties and hotels," Great Eagle said.

"The directors believe that the prospects of the hotel industry in other major cities in the world are bright and will therefore continue to seek on a highly selective basis overseas hotels of good quality and location that offer high initial returns and potential for future growth," it added.
The terms of the offering will be fixed later, Great Eagle said.
It said Tai Shan intended to use about HK$700 million of the net proceeds for the development of a joint venture office and commercial complex in Mongkok, Kowloon.

About HK$826.5 million would be used to repay loans made by Great Eagle to finance the Mongkok project and the balance would be used for the expansion of the office and commercial property portfolio and working capital.

Great Eagle said the public would own 15 percent of Tai Shan after the offering and investors in Citibank Plaza, an office and commercial building in Hong Kong's Central district, would own 11.85 percent after exchanging their interest in Citibank Plaza for Tai Shan shares.
Tai Shan has interests in Great Eagle Centre, Citibank Plaza and the Mongkok project. As of December 31, 1996, Tai Shan's attributable interest in the properties was HK$24.41 billion.
Tai Shan directors expect net profit for the year ending September 30, 1997 of at least HK$970 million compared with net profit of HK$923.02 million for fiscal 1996.
Peregrine Capital Ltd will be the global coordinator and sponsor of the offering.
